evidence: Cic. Div. 2.104: quod dubium contrōversumque sit (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Leg. 1.52: rēs contrōversa et plēna dissēnsiōnis inter doctissimōs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: What is the subject of dispute: a question, a right, a piece of land. It does not mean “quarrelsome” (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Liv. 40.34.14: agrum, quī in contrōversiā erat (Lewis & Short)
Cic. de Or. 2.291: rem in contrōversiam vocāre (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: contrōversia is the dispute itself, a controversy; in contrōversiam venīre is “to become controversial”, in contrōversiam vocāre “to call in question”.
Late Latin; the classical word is contrōversus.

phrases.latin: rēs contrōversa et plēna dissēnsiōnis inter doctissimōs
phrases.english: a controversial matter, full of disagreement among the most learned

phrases.latin: Rēs contrōversa est; nōn omnēs idem sentiunt.
phrases.english: It’s a controversial question; not everyone thinks the same.
